reasons: Deviation classification is correct: although Section 9's cap is facially mutual and excludes consequential damages, the cap base is narrowed to amounts 'actually paid ... for the transaction which the liability relates to', which is materially narrower than 12 months' fees and can fall below the six-month walk-away floor, and the only carve-out is Section 8 (Commerce One's IP indemnity) — the fallback's required carve-outs for confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are absent. The clause therefore fails the fallback on two material terms, not merely on preferred-only refinements.

Redline is actionable and directionally correct for the Customer (Corio): it preserves the mutual structure, replaces the illusory per-transaction base with the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, adds an Excluded Claims definition covering indemnification, confidentiality (Section 10/NDA), gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirms Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages — matching the rule's model language.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.747 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here: the rule requires replacing the cap basis and inserting a carve-out sentence, and the drafter left the exclusion-of-damages sentence and the reasonable-allocation-of-risk sentence intact rather than rewriting the section.
Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, in first person plural, states the playbook position and offers the straight 12-month fee cap fallback conditioned on carve-outs.

Minor, non-disqualifying observations: the surviving consequential-damages sentence still carves out only Section 8 rather than Excluded Claims, and the rationale's aside about garbled text at p0092 is noise with no corresponding edit; neither affects the validity of the finding.
